candidates.title: DEBUG=True reachable in production via non-'True' env spellings — every deploy guard is case/exact-match while Django accepts 'true'/'1'/'yes'/'on'
candidates.description: Three independent gates try to keep DEBUG off in production, and all three compare the raw env string, not the parsed boolean: (1) docker/api/entrypoint.sh runs `check --deploy` only `if [ "$DEBUG" != "True" ]`; (2) the CI deploy preflight greps `^DEBUG=True` in .env; (3) every custom security check (checks.py E001-E005, envguard E006-E018, users.E001-E003) early-returns `if settings.DEBUG`. But settings.py parses `DEBUG = config('DEBUG', default=False, cast=bool)` and python-decouple's bool cast accepts 'true', '1', 'yes', 'on' (case-insensitive) — envguard E017 itself lists exactly these spellings as recognized booleans. So DEBUG=true, DEBUG=1, DEBUG=yes, DEBUG=TRUE, DEBUG=on in .env yields settings.DEBUG=True while: the entrypoint still runs check --deploy (string != 'True') but it passes vacuously because all project checks return [] under DEBUG and Django's own deploy findings are warnings below --fail-level ERROR; the CI grep misses it; urls.py `if settings.DEBUG:` then mounts /api/schema/, /api/docs/swagger/, /api/docs/redoc/, /api-auth/ (browsable API login), and static(MEDIA_URL) — the last serving MEDIA_ROOT including private/ chat attachments that nginx explicitly 404s in prod; technical 500/404 pages expose tracebacks/settings excerpts. On Render there is no CI grep at all, so a dashboard DEBUG flip to any spelling also bypasses everything (exact 'True' skips the check; other spellings run a vacuous one).
candidates.root_cause: Boolean security gates implemented as exact/lowercase-sensitive shell string comparisons (`[ "$DEBUG" != "True" ]`, `grep '^DEBUG=True'`) instead of comparing the parsed settings.DEBUG, while the settings parser (python-decouple cast=bool) accepts a family of truthy spellings. No check anywhere asserts settings.DEBUG is False in production.
candidates.intended_behavior: Any env spelling that Django parses as DEBUG=True must be treated identically by the entrypoint gate, the CI preflight, and a system check — i.e. production must refuse to boot (or at minimum run a check that can actually fail) whenever the effective DEBUG is true.

trace.description: DEBUG = config('DEBUG', default=False, cast=bool) — decouple bool accepts true/1/yes/on any case
if [ "$DEBUG" != "True" ] — only exact 'True' skips check; 'true'/'1'/'yes' run a check that cannot fail
check_production_transport_security returns [] when settings.DEBUG — same early-return in users checks
users.E001/E002/E003 all early-return on settings.DEBUG

if settings.DEBUG: mounts api-auth/, api/schema/, swagger, redoc, and static(MEDIA_URL) — private chat attachments under MEDIA_ROOT/private become web-served, bypassing nginx location ^~ /media/private/ { return 404; }
if grep -q '^DEBUG=True' .env — case-sensitive, misses DEBUG=true/1/yes/TRUE/on; Render path has no equivalent gate

candidates.evidence: settings.py:29 cast=bool; entrypoint.sh:20 exact 'True' compare; ci-cd.yml:480 grep '^DEBUG=True'; checks.py:24 / users/checks.py:18,38 early-return on settings.DEBUG; urls.py:136-145 DEBUG-gated schema/docs/api-auth/media-static; envguard.py:206-211 E017 treats '1','true','yes','on','off' as valid DEBUG spellings (proving the project knows they parse).
candidates.conditions: Operator sets DEBUG to any truthy spelling other than the exact string 'True' in the deploy env (.env on VPS, dashboard on Render). No other precondition — the bypass is deterministic once the value is set.

execution.command: DEBUG=true python manage.py check --deploy --fail-level ERROR  (simulated reasoning; no runtime available in read-only mode)
execution.observed_result: Source-derived: settings.DEBUG=True; all custom security checks return []; Django deploy warnings are below ERROR fail-level; entrypoint proceeds to collectstatic/migrate/gunicorn; urls.py exposes schema/docs/browsable API and serves MEDIA_ROOT including private/ attachments; SECURE_* defaults flip to False (cookies lose Secure, HSTS 0) though nginx still terminates TLS.

candidates.remediation: 1) Normalize once: in entrypoint.sh and the CI grep, test the parsed value (e.g. python -c 'import django; django.setup(); from django.conf import settings; raise SystemExit(0 if settings.DEBUG else 1)' or grep -iE '^DEBUG=(true|1|yes|on)$' case-insensitively plus 'True'). 2) Add an envguard rule: if settings.DEBUG under --deploy context -> error. 3) Make the DEBUG branches in urls.py additionally require an explicit env flag (e.g. SCHEMA_ENABLED) rather than DEBUG alone, so a DEBUG slip doesn't expose schema/docs/media.

severity.rationale: Requires an env misconfiguration, but the entire point of the guard chain is to catch exactly that; three case-sensitive comparisons leave a wide spelling bypass. Impact is full Django debug mode: API schema + browsable-API login exposed, technical error pages, DEBUG-gated MEDIA serving that bypasses the nginx private-attachment block, and all SECURE_* cookie/HSTS defaults silently off. On Render there is no CI grep backstop at all.

candidates.title: StoreSitemap lists stores that fail the public-access gate (missing has_public_link / active-subscription check)
candidates.description: /sitemap.xml is public and unauthenticated. StoreSitemap.items() filters Store.objects only by is_published=True, is_blocked=False, but EVERY public store endpoint (public, public_catalog, public_pattern*, public_contact, reviews, resolve_slug for custom domains) additionally requires profile_has_benefit(store.user, 'has_public_link'), which resolves through plan_benefits_of -> suscription.grants_access() (active, in-vigencia subscription). is_published defaults True, so any store whose owner never paid / let the plan lapse still appears in the sitemap with its slug and lastmod even though its public page returns 404. The sitemap's own docstring claims 'las mismas reglas del endpoint publico' — it does not implement them.
candidates.root_cause: StoreSitemap.items() replicates only the two boolean flags and omits the subscription-benefit gate that the public viewset enforces per-request.
candidates.intended_behavior: Sitemap should only list stores whose public URL actually resolves (is_published AND !is_blocked AND owner has has_public_link benefit via active subscription), matching the public endpoint's 404 rule.

trace.description: items() -> Store.objects.filter(is_published=True, is_blocked=False) — no benefit/subscription filter
path('sitemap.xml', sitemap, ...) — public, no auth/throttle
public() raises Http404 unless profile_has_benefit(store.user,'has_public_link')
plan_benefits_of requires suscription.grants_access() — lapsed/no plan => benefit False => public page 404 but sitemap still lists

candidates.conditions: Any Store row with is_published=True, is_blocked=False whose owner lacks an active subscription granting has_public_link (free/lapsed accounts — the common case since registration no longer creates a subscription).

execution.command: GET /sitemap.xml on a deployment containing lapsed stores
execution.observed_result: Source-derived: sitemap <url> entries for slugs that return 404 on /api/stores/public/<slug>/ and on the SPA store page.

candidates.remediation: Filter StoreSitemap.items() through the same gate — e.g. annotate/exists on the owner's active suscription plan benefits (has_public_link enabled), or reuse a queryset helper shared with the public endpoint.

severity.rationale: Unauthenticated enumeration of store slugs (business names) that are not actually publicly reachable, plus SEO indexing of dead stores. Slugs are low-sensitivity identifiers and the data exposed is just slug+lastmod, but it violates the stated 'same rules as public endpoint' invariant and leaks tenant existence at scale.

candidates.title: RequestIdMiddleware logs raw request.path — percent-encoded control chars forge log lines
candidates.description: RequestIdMiddleware.__call__ ends every request with logger.info('request id=%s %s %s -> %s', ..., request.path, ...). request.path is the URL-decoded PATH_INFO; a request like GET /%0AForged%20log%20entry HTTP/1.1 yields a newline inside the logged path, splitting one access-log record into attacker-shaped lines in stdout (json-file logs, Render logs). Gunicorn/Django do not reject %00-%1F in PATH_INFO before this log runs — the response may be a 404/SPA but the forged line is already emitted. The ScrubSecretsFilter redacts secrets, not control characters.
candidates.root_cause: Untrusted, decoded URL path interpolated into a single-line log record without sanitization/escaping.
candidates.intended_behavior: Log fields derived from request data should be single-line sanitized (strip/replace [\x00-\x1f\x7f]) before emission.

trace.description: logger.info('request id=%s %s %s -> %s (%.0fms)', request.request_id, request.method, request.path, response.status_code, ...)
X-Request-ID is charset-validated (no newline possible) but request.path is not

candidates.evidence: middleware.py:142-144; logscrub.py patterns contain no control-char stripping.
candidates.conditions: Any HTTP client can send percent-encoded CR/LF in the path; gunicorn unquotes PATH_INFO per WSGI convention.

execution.observed_result: Source-derived: decoded newline reaches logger.info -> multi-line log record.

candidates.remediation: Sanitize request.path (and method) in RequestIdMiddleware before logging: re.sub(r'[\x00-\x1f\x7f]', '?', path) or log request.path_info escaped; alternatively move access logging to gunicorn accesslog format which already quotes.

severity.rationale: Log/audit integrity only — forged entries could confuse incident review or hide real attacks in noise; no code execution or data exposure.

candidates.title: PUBLIC_DOMAIN is unsettable in every deploy path — canonical-host redirects and store-domain CNAME verification are hardcoded to 'davent.com.ar'
candidates.description: settings.PUBLIC_DOMAIN = config('PUBLIC_DOMAIN', default='davent.com.ar') feeds two security/functional mechanisms: (a) CanonicalHostMiddleware builds www.<PUBLIC_DOMAIN> -> <PUBLIC_DOMAIN> 301s; (b) StoreDomain verification (services/domains.py public_domain()/check_domain/serialize_domain) tells owners to CNAME their custom domain to PUBLIC_DOMAIN and accepts CNAME targets equal to or ending in '.<PUBLIC_DOMAIN>'. PUBLIC_DOMAIN appears nowhere in docker-compose.yml x-api-env (explicit allowlist), .env.example, or render.yaml envVars — so it is ALWAYS 'davent.com.ar' in both deploys regardless of the real platform domain. The repo's own docs disagree on the domain (.env.example PLATFORM_DOMAIN=davent.com, render.yaml davent.com.ar). If the VPS actually serves davent.com, owners who follow the UI's CNAME instructions point traffic at davent.com.ar (a different deployment/DB — likely Render+Neon), producing verified domains that 400 DisallowedHost or serve the wrong backend; and CanonicalHostMiddleware either never fires or, if PLATFORM_DOMAIN=davent.com.ar, fights the nginx apex->www redirect producing a 301 loop (nginx: apex->www; Django middleware: www->apex).
candidates.claimed_root_cause: PUBLIC_DOMAIN is missing from the compose environment allowlist (x-api-env), .env.example, and render.yaml, so the documented 'env-configurable canonical domain' is unreachable; the hardcoded default 'davent.com.ar' silently wins everywhere.

trace.description: PUBLIC_DOMAIN = config('PUBLIC_DOMAIN', default='davent.com.ar')
x-api-env allowlist contains PLATFORM_DOMAIN but NOT PUBLIC_DOMAIN -> container always sees the default
envVars has no PUBLIC_DOMAIN key
PLATFORM_DOMAIN=davent.com documented; PUBLIC_DOMAIN absent entirely
canonical/alias derived from PUBLIC_DOMAIN -> www.<PUBLIC_DOMAIN> 301s to apex
public_domain() -> settings.PUBLIC_DOMAIN -> CNAME verification target + UI instructions + tls issuance trust chain
nginx apex server 301s to www.${PLATFORM_DOMAIN} — opposite canonical direction to Django's www->apex when domains coincide

candidates.evidence: grep PUBLIC_DOMAIN: only settings.py:36, domains.py:23, middleware.py:243-258, AGENTS.md doc — zero occurrences in compose/.env.example/render.yaml.
candidates.blockers: Actual PLATFORM_DOMAIN and ALLOWED_HOSTS in the VPS .env, and which domain(s) the VPS vs Render deployments actually serve, are not source-visible. The defect (unsettable var + hardcoded default) is source-confirmed; whether it produces a redirect loop, broken CNAME verification, or is coincidentally consistent depends on deployed values.

validation_plan.steps: On the VPS: grep '^PLATFORM_DOMAIN\|^PUBLIC_DOMAIN\|^ALLOWED_HOSTS\|^FRONTEND_URL' /opt/davent/.env; curl -sI https://<apex>/ and https://www.<apex>/ observing 301 targets; check whether 'www.davent.com.ar' or 'www.davent.com' is the live canonical.
validation_plan.expected: If PLATFORM_DOMAIN=davent.com.ar and PUBLIC_DOMAIN unset -> apex->www (nginx) then www->apex (Django) infinite loop. If PLATFORM_DOMAIN=davent.com -> custom-domain CNAME instructions point owners to davent.com.ar (wrong backend).

validation_plan.steps: Render compose config with a test .env: docker compose config | grep -i public_domain (absent); python -c settings.PUBLIC_DOMAIN with env unset -> 'davent.com.ar'.

candidates.title: Django admin unreachable through the VPS web tier for any ADMIN_URL not under /admin/ or /api/ — obfuscation requirement and proxy coverage contradict each other
candidates.description: The compose/VPS deploy requires ADMIN_URL to be non-predictable: users.E001 fails check --deploy for 'admin/', the CI preflight greps it out, and DEPLOY_CHECK_STRICT=1 aborts boot. But the nginx vhost (docker/web/templates/default.conf.template) only proxies /api/ (plus exact /api/token/ rate-limit location) and literal /admin/ to gunicorn; every other path falls to `location / { try_files $uri $uri/ /index.html; }` -> SPA. So with the documented pattern ADMIN_URL=gestion-xxx/ (see .env.example), requests to /gestion-xxx/login/ are answered with index.html — the Django admin is unreachable from the public web entirely (staff would need SSH tunnel to api:8000, or an ADMIN_URL cleverly placed under 'api/' which passes E001 since strip('/')!='admin' but is still guessable). Either the admin is broken-by-deployment (availability/ops failure that pressures admins to weaken controls) or operators discovered the 'api/' prefix workaround. On Render there is no nginx so admin works at whatever ADMIN_URL is set.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: nginx location coverage was written for a literal /admin/ path while the security model requires ADMIN_URL to be a non-obvious env path; no nginx location or envsubst variable maps the configured admin prefix to the API upstream.

trace.description: location /api/ -> proxy; line 118 location /admin/ -> proxy; line 158 location / -> try_files /index.html (SPA)
users.E001: ADMIN_URL.strip('/') in ('','admin') -> deploy error; 'admin/' forbidden
ADMIN_URL=gestion-cambiar-por-un-path-aleatorio/ — such a path matches NO nginx location
path(settings.ADMIN_URL, admin.site.urls) — Django side is correct; only the proxy layer lacks the route
DEPLOY_CHECK_STRICT=1 -> 'admin/' cannot be used to make nginx /admin/ work

candidates.evidence: Template has exactly three proxy locations (/api/, =/api/token/, /admin/); .env.example prescribes an obfuscated path; users.E001 + CI grep + DEPLOY_CHECK_STRICT=1 forbid 'admin/'.
candidates.blockers: The actual ADMIN_URL in the VPS .env is not source-visible; if it happens to be 'api/<something>/' the admin does work through the /api/ proxy (and 'api/admin/' would satisfy E001 while remaining guessable). Whether staff use an SSH tunnel is an ops fact.

validation_plan.steps: grep '^ADMIN_URL' /opt/davent/.env; curl -sk https://<domain>/<ADMIN_URL>login/ -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{content_type}' — expect text/html SPA (200) instead of Django admin login if path isn't under /api/ or /admin/.
validation_plan.expected: SPA index.html response => admin unreachable via web tier.

validation_plan.steps: docker compose config + nginx template review, or run the template through envsubst with PLATFORM_DOMAIN=test and probe /gestion-x/login/.

candidates.title: Caddy edge image builds caddy-dns/cloudflare plugin at unpinned latest — mutable build input into the TLS terminator for all traffic
candidates.description: docker/caddy/Dockerfile runs `xcaddy build --with github.com/caddy-dns/cloudflare --replace golang.org/x/net=golang.org/x/net@v0.62.0`. The --replace pins x/net, but the cloudflare plugin module itself has no @version — xcaddy resolves the latest commit of the module repo at image-build time and produces the caddy binary that becomes the production edge: it terminates TLS for the platform wildcard AND on-demand TLS for every verified customer custom domain, holds CF_API_TOKEN (Zone.DNS), and proxies all HTTP. Any writer to that upstream repo (or a compromised Go module proxy path before sumdb pinning — xcaddy generates a fresh go.mod without a committed go.sum) can land code in the next scheduled/CI image build -> rebuild -> deploy to the edge with full MITM capability over every request including admin sessions and customer PII. Base images caddy:2-builder/caddy:2 are also tag-mutable. Same class: compose `docker compose pull` re-pulls tag-mutable postgres:16-alpine and redis:7.4-alpine on every deploy.
candidates.root_cause: Build input (VCS module + base image tags) not bound to an immutable version/digest; no go.sum committed for the xcaddy module set.
candidates.intended_behavior: Pin the plugin to a release tag/commit (@vX.Y.Z or pseudo-version), commit the resulting go.sum or build via a locked module file, and digest-pin base images (or at least rely on Dependabot docker updates with review).

trace.description: RUN xcaddy build --with github.com/caddy-dns/cloudflare --replace golang.org/x/net=...@v0.62.0 — plugin unpinned
FROM caddy:2 / caddy:2-builder — mutable tags
wildcard *.PLATFORM_DOMAIN tls dns cloudflare {env.CF_API_TOKEN} — the unpinned plugin controls DNS-01 for the wildcard cert
postgres:16-alpine / redis:7.4-alpine tag-mutable, re-pulled by `docker compose pull` each deploy (ci-cd.yml:513)

candidates.evidence: Dockerfile lines 4-11; Caddyfile dns cloudflare usage; ci-cd.yml build-push of caddy image then deploy pull.
candidates.conditions: A malicious/compromised commit lands in caddy-dns/cloudflare (or its dependencies) before the next image build; or a mutable base-image tag is repointed. Requires upstream compromise — likelihood very low, impact maximal (edge MITM + CF token in env).

execution.observed_result: Source-confirmed absence of version pin; xcaddy semantics resolve latest by default.

candidates.remediation: Pin: `xcaddy build --with github.com/caddy-dns/cloudflare@v0.5.0` (or current release) and ideally vendor a go.mod/go.sum; digest-pin caddy:2-builder/caddy:2 bases; consider digest-pinning postgres/redis images or accepting the risk explicitly.

severity.rationale: Classic unpinned-build-input supply-chain gap on the highest-trust component (edge TLS + CF DNS token). Exploitation needs upstream repo compromise; Trivy image scan would not catch a malicious-but-clean Go module. Reported low overall because the trigger is external and the repo otherwise has strong pinning hygiene.

hardening: .gitignore does not cover `.secrets/` — the deploy drops plaintext MP_WEBHOOK_SECRET/SECRET_MP_KEY into /opt/davent/.secrets/ (inside the git working tree) before shredding; a failed run leaves them on disk and `git add -A` on the VPS could commit them. Add `.secrets/` to .gitignore.

First-party/sigstore GitHub actions are tag-pinned (actions/checkout@v7, setup-python@v7, setup-node@v4, docker/setup-buildx-action@v4, docker/login-action@v4, docker/metadata-action@v6, docker/build-push-action@v7, sigstore/cosign-installer@v3) while third-party actions are SHA-pinned — inconsistent; tags are mutable. Consider SHA-pinning all.

cosign signs sha-<commit> images but the VPS deploy (`docker compose pull` + `up`) never verifies signatures — provenance is decorative until `cosign verify` (or registry-level policy) is added to the deploy script.

build job keeps packages:write + id-token:write permissions on pull_request runs; PR-controlled Dockerfile RUN steps execute in that context. For same-repo PRs the token retains declared perms; consider gating elevated permissions to non-PR events.
tblib is installed unpinned in the CI test job (`pip install ... tblib`); pin it like coverage==7.6.10.
requirements.txt has == pins but no --require-hashes; pip-audit+trivy gates exist, so this is defense-in-depth only.

Base images are tag-mutable throughout (python:3.11-slim-bookworm, node:22-alpine, nginxinc/nginx-unprivileged:1.30-alpine, postgres:16-alpine, redis:7.4-alpine, caddy:2*); Dependabot 'docker' entries point at '/' and '/docker' which may not match nested docker/api|web|caddy/Dockerfile — verify dependabot actually proposes base-image updates.

logscrub SECRET_PATTERNS do not cover '*_SECRET'/'*_KEY' names — SECRET_KEY, MP_WEBHOOK_SECRET, SECRETS_MASTER_KEYS, R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, non-PEM AFIP_KEY would pass through unredacted if ever logged. No current call site logs them (grep-verified), so this is a safety-net gap, not an active leak.

envguard E010 false-positives on the legitimate Django CSRF wildcard 'https://*.domain' already present in .env.example — '://*' substring check can't distinguish CORS (no wildcard support) from CSRF (wildcard supported). A verbatim .env.example deploy fails check_env/check --deploy.
envguard E018 exempts any origin containing 'localhost'/'127.0.0.1' — 'http://localhost.evil.com' would slip the prod http check; match host exactly instead of substring.
envguard has no rule requiring DEBUG=False — combined with the spelling bypass (candidate), consider an explicit E-rule or a check that fails whenever settings.DEBUG under --deploy.

ADMIN_URL validation (users.E001 + CI grep) only rejects exact 'admin'/'admin/' — 'Admin/', 'adminx/', ' admin/' pass; require minimum length/entropy or a charset check rather than a denylist of one value.

gunicorn forwarded_allow_ips='*' + api/celery on edge_net: any compromised edge_net container can spoof X-Forwarded-For/Proto to api:8000, bypassing client_ip/throttle/lockout pinning (post-compromise lateral). Restrict forwarded_allow_ips to the nginx/caddy subnet if feasible.

custom_hosts.is_verified_domain_host calls cache.get/cache.set outside the try — a Redis outage 500s all custom-domain/subdomain-foreign hosts (fail-closed but ungraceful); wrap cache ops in the resilient helpers.

compose x-api-env omits PUBLIC_DOMAIN (see candidate), SENTRY_DSN (no error tracking on VPS), and all AI-provider keys (ANTHROPIC/GEMINI/GROQ/OPENROUTER + models) — AI design silently falls back to deterministic script on VPS; consider documenting or wiring intentionally.

tls_ask endpoint is a public oracle revealing whether an arbitrary domain is a verified StoreDomain (customer enumeration, ~1000/h/IP via PublicReadThrottle) and doesn't check store is_published/is_blocked before Caddy issues certs — minor; consider a shared-secret header in the ask URL if Caddy supports it.

render.yaml DEPLOY_CHECK_STRICT=0 means deploy-check violations (e.g. missing SECRETS_MASTER_KEYS -> PII encrypted under kid 'self' becoming unreadable later) only appear in logs; documented tradeoff, but consider alerting on the check output.
vite ^5.4.8 resolves to 5.4.21 — Vite 5 is an EOL major line (devDep, build-time only, excluded from npm audit --omit=dev); plan upgrade to Vite 6/7.
Dockerfile HEALTHCHECK and compose healthchecks hit /healthz/ which returns only {'status':'ok'} — verified no info disclosure; keep it that way.
nginx :8081 vhost uses server_name _ accepting any Host — currently safe because only Caddy edge_net reaches it after tls-ask approval; if edge_net membership ever grows, re-review.

SPA frame-ancestors/CSP allow https://*.${PLATFORM_DOMAIN} — any store subdomain can frame the platform SPA (intended for editor preview); store owners can't inject arbitrary iframes today, but keep an eye on design-pattern HTML capabilities.
